doc: The shapes a provider writes a tool definition in. The canonical form is the server's; every path into a producer's own shape is here. Named for what the file holds rather than for who wrote it, because the five shapes belong to providers rather than to frameworks - which is also why the framework sweep never saw them in Rust: its markers derive from asset ids, and provider names are excluded by design.

tool_shapes.doc: A producer that already writes the canonical wrapper. The function object is taken as it stands rather than re-derived member by member, because re-deriving drops whatever else it carries. `strict` is carried from beside it: it says what the model may send, so losing it changes what the tool permits.

A name beside a JSON Schema under `input_schema`. Refused where a canonical `function` is also present, or this would claim a payload the canonical shape describes better - the ranks alone would not, since a producer may write both members.
tool_shapes.name: $.name

tool_shapes.doc: The definition nested under `toolSpec`, whose schema is written either wrapped in `json` or directly. Both spellings, in that order, because the same producer writes both.
tool_shapes.name: $.toolSpec.name

tool_shapes.doc: One payload holding several declarations. `each` is what makes that expressible: the retired reader looped inside itself, so a payload with several definitions was one reader's private business rather than a declared multiplicity.
tool_shapes.name: $.name

tool_shapes.doc: Arguments as a map from name to facts rather than as a schema. Declared as `argument_map` rather than guessed from the content, which is how a member named `type` inside such a map came to be read as a finished schema. Refused beside `input_schema` or a canonical `function`, both of which describe the same payload more precisely.
tool_shapes.name: $.name
